notYet: Not yet part of the Western Mediterranean

stages.name: Outside the trade
stages.desc: Few or no Gaditan amphorae known in this period

stages.name: Importer of Gaditan amphorae
stages.desc: Salted fish of the Strait reaches its ports

stages.name: Punic producer
stages.desc: Punic cities catch, salt and bottle fish

stages.name: Contested by war
stages.desc: Land where the wars of the age are fought

stages.name: Under Roman control
stages.desc: Provinces, allies and the Republic itself

stages.name: Roman-era fish exporter
stages.desc: Under Rome, salting revives and expands

states.name: Morocco
timeline: Lixus and its neighbours send out amphorae; salting vats themselves are known only later
Kuass fires pottery in the fashion of Gadir for both shores of the Strait
Carthage is gone; the Punic towns live on under the kings of Mauretania
King Bocchus hands Jugurtha to Rome and becomes its ally, not its subject

states.name: Spain
timeline: Gadir and its Phoenician neighbours on the southern coast salt tuna; the interior belongs to other peoples
The salting works of the Bay of Cádiz, such as Las Redes, enter their busiest century
Gadir turns toward Atlantic markets as its amphorae fade from the eastern Mediterranean
Hamilcar Barca lands at Gadir; southern Spain becomes Carthage's war chest
The Second Punic War: Rome and Carthage fight for Spain
Gadir surrenders to Rome, the last Carthaginian base in Spain to fall
Rome organises two Spanish provinces; the old Punic salting works close about now
Fish is salted at Punta Camarinal, beside Baelo on the Strait, in the later second century BC

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage, greatest of the Punic cities, receives amphorae from the Strait
Agathocles of Syracuse invades Carthage's homeland
Peace; Carthage is said to keep the best Atlantic tuna for its own tables
A Roman army under Regulus lands in Africa
Regulus is beaten, and the western trade goes on
Unpaid mercenaries and African subjects rise against Carthage
The revolt is crushed, and Carthage looks to Spain
Scipio invades Africa
Carthage loses its fleet and Spain, but not its merchants
Rome besieges Carthage
Carthage is destroyed and Rome makes the province of Africa

states.name: Greece
timeline: Amphorae from the Strait reach Athens before the Persian sack of 480 BC
Corinth's Punic Amphora Building handles fish from Gadir
The western amphorae have faded from Greek markets, though comedy still knows the name of Gadir
A Strait amphora lies in an Athenian deposit: a thin trade, perhaps through Carthage
Little from the Strait is known in Greece
Rome destroys Corinth; Greece passes under Roman control

states.name: Italy
timeline: Etruscan, Greek and Punic harbours of Italy, Sicily and Sardinia receive Strait amphorae
Salting works in Punic and Greek Sicily take the market; Strait amphorae become scarce
Rome takes Tarentum and controls the Italian peninsula
The First Punic War begins over Messina, in Sicily
Carthage gives up Sicily; Sardinia follows within four years
Hannibal crosses the Alps
Hannibal sails home; Italy and the islands remain Rome's
Fish from the far west returns to Italian tables in growing volume

states.name: Portugal
timeline: Strait amphorae reach the harbours of the Algarve, the Sado and the Tagus
The Algarve fills with amphorae and tableware from Gadir
The Lusitanian War begins: raids, reprisals and Roman massacres
Decimus Junius Brutus campaigns through Lusitania from a base on the Tagus

events.title: Gadir's salters
events.text: Around the Bay of Cádiz, salting works, salt pans and kilns serve a growing export trade.

events.title: Camposoto works
events.text: South of the city, a salting complex founded about a century earlier is still at work.

events.title: Athens burned
events.text: The Persians sack Athens; amphorae from the Strait lie in layers older than the destruction.

events.title: Battle of Himera
events.text: The Greeks of Sicily destroy a Carthaginian army on the island's north coast.

events.title: Pindar's limit
events.text: About now the poet Pindar, praising an athlete of Aegina, names Gadeira as the western limit no one may pass.

events.title: The Lady of Cádiz
events.text: About now a marble coffin with a woman's face, in Phoenician style, is buried at Gadir: a sign of great wealth.

events.title: Punic Amphora Building
events.text: Near Corinth's forum a trading house handles Punic amphorae of salted tuna and sea bream in the mid-fifth century BC.

events.title: Jars at Olympia
events.text: Strait amphorae also reach the sanctuary of Zeus at Olympia in the fifth century BC.

events.title: Lixus
events.text: Morocco's Atlantic port flourishes; some of the jars found at Corinth came from northern Morocco.

events.title: Málaga's potters
events.text: Workshops on the Málaga coast supply part of the jars found at Corinth.

events.title: Las Redes
events.text: About now a salting house works near El Puerto de Santa María, with a sloping paved floor and rooms for amphorae.

events.title: A joke by Eupolis
events.text: In his comedy Marikas, Eupolis jokes about salted fish from Gadir.

events.title: Carthage returns
events.text: A Carthaginian army takes Selinus and Himera, opening a long struggle with Syracuse.

events.title: Tagomago wreck
events.text: About now a ship carrying Strait amphorae sinks off Ibiza.

events.title: Motya destroyed
events.text: Dionysius of Syracuse storms the Punic island city of Motya in western Sicily.

events.title: Sicilian rivals
events.text: Solunto and Panormus in Punic Sicily, and Greek towns around Syracuse, build salting works that compete with the west.

events.title: The Gaditan Algarve
events.text: Castro Marim and its neighbours fill with amphorae and tableware from Gadir.

events.title: Treaty with Rome
events.text: Rome and Carthage agree limits on Roman trading and settling in the western seas.

events.title: The Atlantic road
events.text: Gaditan wares travel up the coast to Galicia, probably in exchange for gold and tin.

events.title: Tyre falls
events.text: Alexander storms Gadir's mother city in the east; some Tyrians are said to find refuge at Carthage.

events.title: Kuass pottery
events.text: Kilns on the Moroccan coast make red tableware inspired by Greek wares for the Strait's towns.

events.title: Agathocles in Africa
events.text: Syracuse's ruler lands at Cape Bon to carry the war to Carthage.

events.title: Four days west
events.text: A Greek author says sailors of Gadeira find giant tuna four days beyond the Pillars and salt them for Carthage.

events.title: Tuna on coins
events.text: About now Gadir strikes coins that show Melqart and tuna.

events.title: War over Messina
events.text: Rome and Carthage begin their first war over the strait of Messina.

events.title: Battle of the Aegates
events.text: Rome destroys a Carthaginian fleet off western Sicily, and the First Punic War ends.

events.title: Hamilcar lands
events.text: Hamilcar Barca brings an army to Gadir and begins the conquest of southern Spain.

events.title: New Carthage
events.text: Hasdrubal founds a capital at Cartagena, beside silver mines and a great harbour.

events.title: Hannibal's vows
events.text: Before marching on Italy, Hannibal makes vows at the temple of Melqart near Gadir.

events.title: Cannae
events.text: Hannibal destroys a Roman army in Apulia.

events.title: Scipio takes Cartagena
events.text: The Roman general seizes Carthage's Spanish capital.

events.title: Battle of Ilipa
events.text: Scipio defeats Carthage's armies in Spain, north of today's Seville.

events.title: Gadir surrenders
events.text: Shut out of the city, Mago crucifies its magistrates and sails away; Gadir surrenders to Rome.

events.title: Zama
events.text: Scipio defeats Hannibal in Africa, and the Second Punic War soon ends.

events.title: Carteia
events.text: Rome founds a Latin colony on the Bay of Algeciras for thousands of sons of soldiers and Spanish women.

events.title: Cato's complaint
events.text: Cato complains that Romans pay three hundred drachmas for a jar of salted fish from the Black Sea.

events.title: Carthage destroyed
events.text: Rome razes Carthage and sells its survivors into slavery.

events.title: Corinth destroyed
events.text: In the same year the Romans sack Corinth, kill its men and sell its women and children.

events.title: Viriathus murdered
events.text: Rome bribes envoys of the Lusitanian leader, who kill him in his sleep.

events.title: Salting at Baelo
events.text: At Punta Camarinal, beside the later town of Baelo, fish is salted in the later second century BC.

events.title: The little horses
events.text: About now fishermen of Gades sail boats called horses as far as the river Lixus.

events.title: Jugurtha betrayed
events.text: King Bocchus of Mauretania hands Jugurtha to Rome's officer Sulla.

events.title: Treaty renewed
events.text: The Roman Senate confirms its alliance with Gades.

events.title: Balbus the Roman
events.text: Pompey gives Roman citizenship to Balbus of Gades, who later becomes an adviser to Caesar.

events.title: The Titan wreck
events.text: About now a ship carrying southern Spanish fish amphorae sinks off southern France.

chartNote: Share of the area of six present-day countries, by each one's main role in the fish trade of the Strait. A simplification: boundaries are today's, the Punic cities held only coastal strips, and one colour stands for a whole country. 'Importer' means Strait amphorae are known from some sites there, not that everyone ate the fish. Most dates are archaeological and good only to a generation or so.
